title: Certified Azimuth CRB Outage and Power Bounds for Passive RIS-Assisted ISAC Under Partial Echo Attenuation
content: Partial loss of the direct echo can make a prescribed azimuth-accuracy requirement unattainable in passive reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). We bound the sensing Fisher information over all admissible transmit factors and RIS commands. Feasible quantized designs and Swerling-I averaging complete the outage and power brackets. The refined certificate rules out seven additional conditions on a 468-condition grid, with three decisions confirmed on independent trajectories. A two-column rotation can raise sum rate while preserving the full waveform-averaged sensing Fisher information. Under full information at 50 dBm and a 1∘ root Cramér–Rao bound (CRB) target, seven of nine joint cases meet the 5% modeled-outage budget by a pointwise bootstrap criterion. On replay of the original test trajectories, weighted minimum mean-square error refinement with a Fisher-information check increases mean sum rate by 0.030–0.456 bit/s/Hz relative to pair rotation. On fresh trajectories, imperfect design information raises near-target pair-rotation modeled outage from 2.91% to 8.58%. The corresponding fraction of absolute angle errors above 1∘ is 67.08%. In the sensing benchmark with two allowed switches, Kalman-filtered Fisher information scores yield lower modeled outage than recurrent distributional reinforcement learning.
